title: Azion Web Platform
description:
GLOBAL SITE CHROME (every site page): dark-only theme — pure black #000 page, white text, muted grey secondary text, Azion orange #F3652B accent; the site has no light theme (prefers-color-scheme is ignored). Content sits in a centred ~1386px framed column whose left/right edges are 1px hairline rules with small square 'registration mark' dots at section corners; sections are separated by ~190px 'section-gap' spacer bands filled with a fine vertical hatch pattern. Eyebrows are monospace uppercase labels prefixed by an orange '//' (e.g. '// CACHE'). Buttons: small white-filled primary ('Start free'), dark/outline secondary with a '›' chevron ('Talk to a specialist ›', 'Docs ›'); orange-filled only in the nav. Textures: dotted grids behind heroes, orange 'pixelate' dot gradients under illustrations. TOP NAV (56px, sticky, hides on scroll down): orange italic AZION wordmark left; mega-menu triggers 'Solutions', 'Products', 'Developer', 'Resources' (chevrons) and a plain 'Pricing' link; right: 'Contact' text link, 'Login' (white small button), 'Start for free' (orange small button), square search icon button. Mega-menus: Solutions = Application Development, Performance and Reliability, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Application Security, Media and Streaming, Financial Services, Technology, Retail (icon + title + one-line description); Products = 21 products in groups (Functions, Cache, Application Accelerator, Image Processor, AI Inference, Durable Objects, Orchestrator, SQL Database, Object Storage, KV Store, WAF, Bot Manager, Network Shield, Edge DNS, Load Balancer, Secure Internet Access, AI Gateway, Data Stream, Real-Time Events, Edge Pulse, Our Network); Developer = Azion Docs, Guides, Dev Tools, Release Notes, API Reference, Join our community; Resources = Blog, Resource Hub, Success Stories, Partners, Marketplace, Support, Professional Services. iPhone (393px): nav = hamburger + wordmark + orange 'Start for free' + search icon; the hamburger opens a full-height drawer with the same groups as accordions. FOOTER: 4 link columns with muted headings — Company (About us, Our Network, Careers, Compliance, Privacy Policy, Hey AI, learn about us), Resources (Blog, Resource Hub, Learning, Marketplace, Success cases, Recognition and Awards), Getting Started (Start for free, How to start, Pricing, Contact, Professional Services, Scale-Up Program), Developer (Documentation, API, Our Community ↗, Release Notes); bottom bar: wordmark + social icon links (GitHub, LinkedIn, YouTube, X, Instagram, Discord) left, green dot 'All Systems Operational' + globe 'EN' language select right. On iPhone the columns become a 2-column grid and the bottom bar stacks. Cookie banner and HubSpot chat launcher were dismissed/removed before capture (third-party overlays, not part of the design). Marquees/carousels are frozen mid-scroll in the shots.

HUB/COMPANY PAGE: built from the same section vocabulary as product pages (hero band or form hero, framed grids, media splits, quotes, marquees, closing CTA). See the structure below for the exact sequence.

PAGE NOTES (from the previous battery, verified against the new capture): PAGE (1440 full height ≈9400px): 1) HERO (full-width, ~380px tall, black with a dotted-grid band behind the lower half): centred 2-line H1 ~48px — line 1 'Invisible infrastructure' in orange, line 2 'for the speed of AI' in white; 3-line muted subtitle 'Compute, AI, data, security, and observability primitives that run autonomously and scale instantly on 100+ data centers worldwide. One platform, from idea to mission-critical.'; two buttons side by side: 'Start free' (white filled) and 'Talk to a specialist ›' (dark outline). 2) LOGO STRIP: mono uppercase caption 'PROVEN ON MISSION-CRITICAL WORKLOADS' then a horizontally auto-scrolling marquee of greyscale customer logos (NZN, Netshoes, Caixa, agibank, prime video, Madeira Madeira, GPA, Fourbank, GFG, HeroSpark…). 3) PRIMITIVES GRID: centred H2 'Serverless AI-native primitives for autonomous workloads' (2 lines, ~36px) above a bordered 4-column table-like grid (column header row with orange mono labels COMPUTE / AI / DATA / SECURITY). Each cell lists items as icon + bold title + one-line muted description: Compute = Functions, Durable Objects, Rules Engine, Load Balancer, Image Processor; AI = AI Inference, AI Gateway; Data = Object Storage, SQL Database, KV Store, Cache; Security = Web Application Firewall, API Gateway, Bot Manager, DNS. Items are links (rendered as nav 'Platform primitives'). 4) NETWORK BAND (~700px): left text — eyebrow '// REGION: EARTH.', H2 'One distributed infrastructure without the complexity of managing, securing, and scaling it', mono caption 'BUILT AROUND YOUR USERS. DISTRIBUTED AROUND YOUR DATA.', and 4 outlined orange pill stats (100+ data centers, 100+ Tbps network capacity, 30 ms median latency, 100% availability); right — dot-matrix map of the Americas with orange highlighted dots. Below it a 4-column row of customer proof cards (logo + sentence with bold metric): Dafiti '86% faster load times, with a 45% cost reduction in data transfer'; MadeiraMadeira '90% lower cloud costs and faster applications at scale'; Renner '67% saved on data transfer…'; Fourbank 'DDoS mitigated on applications and APIs…'. 5) WHY AZION: eyebrow '// WHY AZION', H2 'From commit to observability, on one platform', subtitle; then 4 equal cells each with a dark illustration (branch diagram main/stage/preview/production; key table PREVIEW/TEST/PROD with active/revoked/expired statuses; orange Azion glyph tile in a circuit; bar chart 1w–6w with orange highlight) and a caption whose first sentence is bold: 'Build at AI speed.', 'Secure by default.', 'No ops required.', 'Faster and more efficient workloads.'. 6) USE-CASE ROWS: 5 stacked 2-column rows (text left, illustration right on a dotted orange gradient): 'Modern applications' (terminal card with framework icons and AZION INIT/BUILD/DEPLOY chips), 'Optimized workloads' (browser mock with 'WWW.YOURSITE.COM SECURE' and a green '99' score ring), 'AI applications' (Azion tile connected to AI provider icons), 'Protected applications and APIs' (4 icon tiles), 'Media and streaming content' (map with icon tiles); each has H3 ~28px, 2-line description and a small outline 'Learn more ›' button. 7) RECOGNITION: eyebrow '// RECOGNITION AND AWARDS', H2 'Recognized as a market leader', then a horizontally auto-scrolling carousel of ~470px quote cards (logo G2/GigaOm/Frost & Sullivan, quote mark, quote text, orange mono source label like 'G2 WINTER 2026 REPORTS'). 8) CLIENT STORIES: mosaic grid — large photo card 'Netshoes automatically blocks more than 4 million threats in six months' + 'Learn more ›', medium photo card GPA 'Grupo Pão de Açúcar (GPA) stops a cyberattack and reduces costs by 30%', and logo tiles (Dafiti on white, agibank on black, Renner black, Fourbank orange, exame black, NZN orange). 9) CLOSING CTA: dotted orange gradient background, centred H2 'Build, secure, and scale applications everywhere.', subtitle 'Get faster launches, lower latency, and less infrastructure overhead from day one.', 'Start free' + 'Talk to a specialist ›'. 10) Footer. Mobile 390: single column; hero buttons full-width stacked; primitives grid becomes one column with each category label as a divider; map band stacks text over map; stats/cards stack.

title: Contact Azion

  h2 "Frequently Asked Questions"
  h3 "What is AI Gateway?"
  p "AI Gateway is one endpoint between your applications and the AI models they call, built on the Azion Web Platform. It authenticates each team, picks a model by policy, falls back when a call fails, caches responses the caller allows, and writes a usage and audit log line for every call. It runs as a function on Azion's distributed infrastructure, behind Firewall."
  h3 "What is AI Gateway built with?"
  p "Functions runs the gateway logic on an application, and AI Inference runs the models hosted on Azion. Firewall applies WAF, rate limits, and DDoS Protection before a request reaches the function. KV Store holds team keys and policies, the Cache API stores allowed responses, and Connectors reach your own model servers. Real-Time Events, Real-Time Metrics, and Data Stream record and export every cal…"
  h3 "Which models and providers can I use?"
  p "Any model on AI Inference, including Qwen3 30B A3B, GPT-OSS 20B, and Mistral 3 Small, plus embedding, reranking, and vision models. The gateway also calls third-party providers whose APIs accept the OpenAI chat completions format, and your own model servers through Connectors. For a provider with its own request format, adapt the request in the function."
  h3 "Do I need to change my application code?"
  p "Usually only the base URL and the key. The gateway accepts OpenAI chat completions requests at /v1/chat/completions, so OpenAI SDKs and compatible clients keep working. Teams send a model alias, such as general, and the platform team decides which model answers it."
  h3 "How does fallback work?"
  p "Each alias has an ordered list of models. When a call throws an error, returns no choices, answers with an error status, or runs past its timeout, the gateway tries the next model. Every failed attempt is logged, and if all of them fail, the gateway answers 502."
  h3 "How do I control spend per team?"
  p "Every call logs the team and the tokens the model used, so your analytics platform can sum spend per team. When a team reaches its budget, set its status to blocked, and the gateway answers 429 to its key. Third-party calls use your own provider keys, so providers bill your accounts at their own prices, with no markup from Azion."
  h3 "How are provider keys and team keys protected?"
  p "Provider keys are stored as secret environment variables and read inside the function, so they never appear in code or reach a team. Each team gets its own gateway key, and KV Store keeps only its SHA-256 hash. To validate JSON Web Tokens instead, run the JWT function from Marketplace on Firewall."
  h3 "How do I monitor requests, latency, and errors?"
  p "Real-Time Metrics charts requests, status codes, upstream status, and function invocations. Real-Time Events keeps each request's log lines for 7 days, grouped by request ID. Data Stream sends the same lines to Splunk, Datadog, Elasticsearch, Google BigQuery, Amazon S3, Apache Kafka, or any HTTPS endpoint."
  h3 "How does AI Gateway on Azion compare to other AI gateways?"
  p "Managed AI gateways give you a fixed set of features to configure. On Azion, the gateway is code you own: routing, fallback, caching, and authentication live in one function, so you can apply any policy your teams need. The same platform runs models on AI Inference and protects the endpoint with Firewall, so there's no separate proxy to secure."
  h3 "What do I need to get started?"
  p "An application with Application Accelerator, which lets a rule run the gateway function, and KV Store, which is in Preview and enabled through Technical Support. The documentation covers the full setup, from the function code to the usage stream. Talk to a specialist to plan the models, routes, and budgets for your teams."

Content sits in a centred ~1386px framed column whose left/right edges are 1px hairline rules with small square 'registration mark' dots at section corners; sections are separated by ~190px 'section-gap' spacer bands filled with a fine vertical hatch pattern. Eyebrows are monospace uppercase labels prefixed by an orange '//' (e.g. '// CACHE'). Buttons: small white-filled primary ('Start free'), dark/outline secondary with a '›' chevron ('Talk to a specialist ›', 'Docs ›'); orange-filled only in the nav. Textures: dotted grids behind heroes, orange 'pixelate' dot gradients under illustrations. TOP NAV (56px, sticky, hides on scroll down): orange italic AZION wordmark left; mega-menu triggers 'Solutions', 'Products', 'Developer', 'Resources' (chevrons) and a plain 'Pricing' link; right: 'Contact' text link, 'Login' (white small button), 'Start for free' (orange small button), square search icon button. Mega-menus: Solutions = Application Development, Performance and Reliability, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Application Security, Media and Streaming, Financial Services, Technology, Retail (icon + title + one-line description); Products = 21 products in groups (Functions, Cache, Application Accelerator, Image Processor, AI Inference, Durable Objects, Orchestrator, SQL Database, Object Storage, KV Store, WAF, Bot Manager, Network Shield, Edge DNS, Load Balancer, Secure Internet Access, AI Gateway, Data Stream, Real-Time Events, Edge Pulse, Our Network); Developer = Azion Docs, Guides, Dev Tools, Release Notes, API Reference, Join our community; Resources = Blog, Resource Hub, Success Stories, Partners, Marketplace, Support, Professional Services. iPhone (393px): nav = hamburger + wordmark + orange 'Start for free' + search icon; the hamburger opens a full-height drawer with the same groups as accordions. FOOTER: 4 link columns with muted headings — Company (About us, Our Network, Careers, Compliance, Privacy Policy, Hey AI, learn about us), Resources (Blog, Resource Hub, Learning, Marketplace, Success cases, Recognition and Awards), Getting Started (Start for free, How to start, Pricing, Contact, Professional Services, Scale-Up Program), Developer (Documentation, API, Our Community ↗, Release Notes); bottom bar: wordmark + social icon links (GitHub, LinkedIn, YouTube, X, Instagram, Discord) left, green dot 'All Systems Operational' + globe 'EN' language select right. On iPhone the columns become a 2-column grid and the bottom bar stacks. Cookie banner and HubSpot chat launcher were dismissed/removed before capture (third-party overlays, not part of the design). Marquees/carousels are frozen mid-scroll in the shots.

HUB/COMPANY PAGE: built from the same section vocabulary as product pages (hero band or form hero, framed grids, media splits, quotes, marquees, closing CTA). See the structure below for the exact sequence.

Content sits in a centred ~1386px framed column whose left/right edges are 1px hairline rules with small square 'registration mark' dots at section corners; sections are separated by ~190px 'section-gap' spacer bands filled with a fine vertical hatch pattern. Eyebrows are monospace uppercase labels prefixed by an orange '//' (e.g. '// CACHE'). Buttons: small white-filled primary ('Start free'), dark/outline secondary with a '›' chevron ('Talk to a specialist ›', 'Docs ›'); orange-filled only in the nav. Textures: dotted grids behind heroes, orange 'pixelate' dot gradients under illustrations. TOP NAV (56px, sticky, hides on scroll down): orange italic AZION wordmark left; mega-menu triggers 'Solutions', 'Products', 'Developer', 'Resources' (chevrons) and a plain 'Pricing' link; right: 'Contact' text link, 'Login' (white small button), 'Start for free' (orange small button), square search icon button. Mega-menus: Solutions = Application Development, Performance and Reliability, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Application Security, Media and Streaming, Financial Services, Technology, Retail (icon + title + one-line description); Products = 21 products in groups (Functions, Cache, Application Accelerator, Image Processor, AI Inference, Durable Objects, Orchestrator, SQL Database, Object Storage, KV Store, WAF, Bot Manager, Network Shield, Edge DNS, Load Balancer, Secure Internet Access, AI Gateway, Data Stream, Real-Time Events, Edge Pulse, Our Network); Developer = Azion Docs, Guides, Dev Tools, Release Notes, API Reference, Join our community; Resources = Blog, Resource Hub, Success Stories, Partners, Marketplace, Support, Professional Services. iPhone (393px): nav = hamburger + wordmark + orange 'Start for free' + search icon; the hamburger opens a full-height drawer with the same groups as accordions. FOOTER: 4 link columns with muted headings — Company (About us, Our Network, Careers, Compliance, Privacy Policy, Hey AI, learn about us), Resources (Blog, Resource Hub, Learning, Marketplace, Success cases, Recognition and Awards), Getting Started (Start for free, How to start, Pricing, Contact, Professional Services, Scale-Up Program), Developer (Documentation, API, Our Community ↗, Release Notes); bottom bar: wordmark + social icon links (GitHub, LinkedIn, YouTube, X, Instagram, Discord) left, green dot 'All Systems Operational' + globe 'EN' language select right. On iPhone the columns become a 2-column grid and the bottom bar stacks. Cookie banner and HubSpot chat launcher were dismissed/removed before capture (third-party overlays, not part of the design). Marquees/carousels are frozen mid-scroll in the shots.

HUB/COMPANY PAGE: built from the same section vocabulary as product pages (hero band or form hero, framed grids, media splits, quotes, marquees, closing CTA). See the structure below for the exact sequence.

Therefore, reinforcing our commitment to this subject, this PRIVACY POLICY (or simply “Policy”) governs the manner in which Azion collects, uses, stores, and discloses information collected from users (individually, “User”) across all content in connection with activities, Products and Services, functions, or features that we provide …"
  h2 "Personal data processed and collection methods"

Data may be collected in the following ways: (a) if you provide it through platform registration, subscription to our products and services, newsletter s…"

  p "Personal data processing may serve the following purposes:"
  list (8): Improve our Products and Services; · Enhance Content; · Conduct promotions, contests, surveys, or other Content features; · Send periodic emails to respond to your questions, inquiries, or other requests; · Offer more targeted services and advertisements, making your visit to Azion’s website more productive; · Keep Products secure and protected; · Make suggestions for you and other users to improve and personalize your experience; · Internal operations, including error correction, data analysis, testing, research, development, and service improvement.
  p "All these operations will always be based on authorized legal grounds, including but not limited to contract execution and preliminary procedures, compliance with legal obligations, regular exercise of rights in processes or contracts, credit protection, serving Azion’s or third parties’ legitimate interests, and fraud prevention. In other cases, personal data processing will be conditional upon t…"
  p "If you no longer wish to receive marketing communications from Azion, you may unsubscribe directly through the unsubscribe link included in emails or by contacting privacy@azion.com ."
  h2 "Data sharing"
  p "Azion does not share, sell, or disclose your personal information except as described in this Policy. Your data, however, may be disclosed (i) if the company is required to do so by law, regulation, or legal process — for example, a court order or subpoena; (ii) in response to requests from government agencies, such as law enforcement authorities; (iii) with your express authorization; (iv) after …"
  h2 "Data retention periods"
  p "Azion will maintain data for as long as users and visitors maintain a relationship with the company. After termination of this relationship, Azion may continue to maintain data due to legal obligations or the company’s legitimate interest, to help respond to legal demands and/or audits and for other causes, such as combating fraud and responding to regulatory agency requests."
  h2 "Data subject rights"
  p "Azion guarantees each data subject the full exercise of rights provided under the applicable laws and regulations applicable to data protection and privacy. This includes: confirming the existence of personal data processing; accessing one’s own data; correcting incomplete, inaccurate, or outdated information; requesting anonymization, blocking, or elimination of unnecessary, excessive, or imprope…"
  p "To exercise any of these rights, send your request to dpo@azion.com (“Rights Request”). Before fulfilling the request, we may request additional information to verify that the requesting person is indeed the data subject in question, thus ensuring information security and confidentiality."
  p "If you are submitting a Rights Request on behalf of another person as an authorized agent, we require that: (a) the data subject verify their identity and confirm directly with Azion that they granted permission to the authorized agent to submit the Rights Request; (b) the authorized agent possess a power of attorney granted by the data subject, in accordance with the legislation of the data subje…"
  h2 "Personal data security"
  p "Azion employs technical and administrative measures, with the security standard usually adopted by the market for personal data protection, suitable to protect users’ and visitors’ personal data against unauthorized access and against accidental or unlawful situations of destruction, loss, alteration, communication, or dissemination."
  p "Likewise, personal information of customers, users, and visitors is restricted access only to employees or parties who need the data for execution and performance of their duties."
  h2 "Privacy Policy updates"
  p "Azion may periodically modify the terms of this Privacy Policy at any time, publishing a revised version on Azion’s website. Modified documents will take effect immediately upon publication."
  h2 "How to contact Azion"
  p "In case of questions or comments about this Privacy Policy, or if you are a data subject and want to exercise your rights and access more information about personal data processing by the company, send an email to Azion’s Data Protection Officer (DPO) at dpo@azion.com ."
  h2 "Change in control"
  p "If Azion’s ownership is acquired by third parties, we may transfer your information to the new owner so they can continue operating Azion’s website, remaining obligated, however, to honor the commitments we made in this Privacy Policy."
  h2 "International data transfer"
  p "Your data may be processed on servers located outside Brazil, in countries where Azion or its providers maintain infrastructure. In these situations, we apply adequate safeguards — including standard contractual clauses, encryption, and access controls — to ensure a level of protection equivalent to that required by applicable regulations."
  h2 "Cookies"
  p "Content may use “cookies” to enhance user experience. The User’s browser stores cookies on their hard drive to maintain records and sometimes track information about them. Users may choose to configure their browser to refuse cookies or alert them when cookies are sent. If they do so, note that some parts of the Content may not function properly."
  h2 "Application of Terms of Use"
  p "The Terms of Use of all Azion virtual environments will be applicable, where appropriate, to this Privacy Policy."
